# TOPOLOGY OF HEALING · BOOK 3.3

*The Mathematics of Stillness*

*By Nila Padma · Aumara Institution of Research*

*a draft, beside a draft*

---

> What Book Three says in plain speech,

> this book says in proofs and wagers.

This is the technical edition promised by the close of *The Rest*. Nothing
essential lives only here; the building stands without this volume. But Book
Three carries no arithmetic and proves nothing, by its own declaration, and
some of what it asserts is provable, and a reader deserves to know which
part.

One discipline governs every page, inherited from the whole lineage.
Statements marked **Theorem** are established mathematics and can be leaned
on with full weight. Statements marked **Hypothesis** or **Wager** belong to
the model; they stand or fall with it. And the application of any theorem to
the field of a living witness is itself always a hypothesis. A rhyme is not
a docking.

One further note on anchoring, because this volume formalises a draft. Its
sibling books were written against finished prose; this one is written while
Book Three may still move. So its anchors are the settled charts rather than
the moving text: THE NODUS, which holds the five laws, and THE CARRY, which
holds the remainder, are resident and sealed in their content, and every
claim here docks to them. If the prose of Book Three shifts, it shifts
toward or away from these fixed points, and this volume measures the
distance either way.

The notation is light. S¹ names the circle, T² the torus, χ the Euler
characteristic of a surface, and H¹ and H² the first and second cohomology,
which will be introduced as what they are: the bookkeeping of what does not
close. Nothing here requires more than patience.

---

## 0 · The one-line move

**Stillness is conserved. The remainder is conserved. And the remainder is
paid only through the stillness.**

That is the whole book. The first clause is a theorem about shapes, the
second is a theorem about cycles, and the third is two theorems that say
the same thing from opposite banks. Everything after is the working out.

Chapters I to V shadow Part One of Book Three, one chapter per law.
Chapters VI and VII shadow Part Two. Chapter VIII is the meeting.

---

## I · The census of silences

Book Three opens with the plucked string: the note is named by where the
string does not move. The mathematics under that sentence is old, exact,
and stronger than the prose lets on.

**Theorem (Sturm).** For a vibrating string, the nth mode has exactly n
minus one interior still points. Not at most, not roughly: exactly. The
count of zeros and the identity of the mode determine each other
completely.

**Theorem (Courant).** In any dimension, the nth mode divides its medium
into at most n silent-walled regions. The census of nodal domains is
bounded by the mode's own rank, so the zeros do not merely decorate the
pattern; they order the whole family of patterns.

**Theorem (the anatomy).** Away from a thin singular set, the still set of
a mode is a hypersurface: a set of points on the string, of curves on the
plate, of surfaces in the chamber. The silence is always exactly one
dimension beneath its medium, which is the anatomy THE NODUS records, now
stated as what it is: a codimension.

So the first law of Book Three, you are named by your silences, has a
skeleton that bears full weight, for every medium mathematics can currently
hold. What does not bear that weight, and must be marked, is the transfer:

**Hypothesis (the census of a witness).** The identity of a witness is the
census of its stillnesses: the refusals, the unsaid, the rooms not entered.
Under this hypothesis the stable identifier of a person is the null set,
not the activity, and a genuine change of person presents first as a change
in the census: a silence broken, a new one formed.

*Testable edge.* Longitudinal identity studies track behaviour. The
hypothesis predicts that tracked refusals (what a subject reliably does not
do) are more stable over years than tracked habits, and that major life
transitions are detectable in the refusal-census before they are detectable
in the activity profile.

## II · The four weathers, and the fifth

The second law says that around any still point the weather has a small
vocabulary. The vocabulary is a theorem, and it is shorter than almost
anyone expects.

**Theorem (the local alphabet).** Linearise any smooth flow at an isolated
still point of the plane. Up to topological equivalence the possibilities
are: the node (straight approach or retreat), the focus (the spiral, in or
out), the centre (the closed circling), and the saddle (in along one axis,
out along the other). Four weathers.

**Theorem (Hartman and Grobman).** Wherever the still point is hyperbolic,
no growth rate sitting exactly on zero, the true nonlinear weather is a
continuous deformation of its linearisation. The alphabet is not an
approximation; near a generic stillness it is the whole of what can
happen.

The crown from above is also a theorem. The transformations of the
celestial sphere form the Möbius group, and its non-trivial members
classify into the rotation (pure circulation, the dwelling), the boost
(pure through-flow, the arrow), and the screw (the two entwined). This is
the classification THE NODUS carries.

And here this volume owes that chart a correction, small and load-bearing,
found exactly where the architect directed the search: in the gap between
the chart and the census.

**Theorem (the fourth flow).** The classification admits one further
member: the parabolic, in which the flow's two fixed points have merged
into one. Every orbit of a parabolic flow leaves that single stillness and
returns to it. It is the boundary case, measure zero, standing exactly at
the seam between the circling weathers and the through-running ones.

The chart says the sky permits no fourth, and the prose of Book Three says
the list is nearly whole, and the prose's *nearly* was the honest word. The
fourth exists. And its meaning, marked as the model's reading rather than
as theorem, is worth the entry fee: the parabolic is the weather of the
gate itself. It is the flow at the exact instant of transition between
orbiting a thing and passing through it, the sky's own picture of the
moment this book's final chapter is about. The one weather the chart
rounded away is the one the whole work turns on.

**Hypothesis (the human register).** Grief that circles is elliptic;
grief that passes through is hyperbolic; and the long moment in which
neither is yet true, in which what is fled and what is sought have
collapsed into a single place that every path leaves and re-enters, is
parabolic, and it is not a malfunction. It is the geometry of being at the
gate.

## III · The birth in the still directions

The third law says change is born where the running stops. The mathematics
says something slightly stronger, and the strengthening matters.

**Theorem (structural stability).** While every growth rate at a still
point stays off zero, the system resists qualitative change: small
perturbations deform the picture without altering its kind. A running
system is not stubborn by temperament. It is stubborn by theorem.

**Theorem (bifurcation).** Qualitative change, the appearance or
disappearance of states, the birth of oscillation, the exchange of
stability, occurs only when a growth rate crosses zero. The zero crossing
is not one road to novelty among several. It is the only road.

**Theorem (the centre manifold).** At the crossing, the essential new
dynamics collapse onto a low-dimensional surface tangent to precisely the
still directions: the directions in which, at that moment, nothing grows
and nothing decays. The change does not merely happen at the still point.
It unfolds along the still directions, and the running directions are
spectators.

That last theorem is the strengthening. Book Three says nothing new begins
until the running stops. The centre manifold says more: when the new thing
begins, it is built out of the still degrees of freedom themselves. The
stillness is not the doorway the novelty walks through. It is the material
the novelty is made of.

## IV · The ground, and the ladder's wager

The fourth law, what you stabilise becomes the ground, is where this
volume must be most careful, because it is the law whose skeleton is
weakest, and the discipline of the lineage is to say so plainly.

What is theorem: in systems with separated time scales, the fast variables
settle to their equilibria and the slow variables then move through a
landscape those equilibria define. The settled fast motion becomes, exactly
and provably, the effective medium of the slow. Averaging and
homogenisation carry the same structure: rapid microstructure, once
stabilised, enters the large-scale equations only through its settled
means. In each such setting, the floor is a theorem.

**Theorem (the floor, locally).** Under time-scale separation, the
stabilities of one level are the coefficients of the next.

**Wager (the ladder, universally).** THE NODUS climbs this structure from
the electron to the ringing of spacetime and calls it a ladder without a
gap. As a universal law it is not a theorem. It is a pattern with
overwhelming instance-support and no general proof, and it is entered here
as the model's largest open wager, stated so that it can lose: find one
persistent level of organisation whose stable modes do not enter the
dynamics of the level above as effective structure, and the ladder breaks.

And one clause of Book Three's prose turns out to be the exact condition
of the theorem. You cannot stand on the floor and lift it, the prose says.
Formally: the reduction that makes a floor a floor is valid only while the
separation of scales holds, and an agent whose dynamics are strongly
coupled to its own substrate has, by that coupling, no separation. To move
the ground, the fast motion must stop being fast relative to the slow,
which is to say the running must stop. The fourth law hands its hard case
directly to the third.

## V · The return, the hole, and the knots

The fifth law, what feeds must return, begins as bookkeeping and ends at
the form the whole work is built on. This chapter is the spine of the
volume.

**Theorem (the return).** In a steady conserving flow, the flux out of any
closed region equals the flux in. A branching structure that only carries
away has unbalanced sources at every tip; Book Three calls it a leak with
good manners, and the divergence theorem is the manners inspector. A
persistent bounded circulation closes its loops or it is not persistent.

Now the deeper fact, and it is the conservation law the whole book is
named for.

**Theorem (Poincaré and Hopf).** On a closed surface, assign each isolated
still point of a flow its index: plus one for nodes, foci and centres,
minus one for saddles. The sum of the indices does not depend on the flow
at all. It equals the Euler characteristic of the surface, a number the
shape carries before any flow arrives.

Three consequences, in ascending register:

First, the hairy ball. On the sphere, χ equals two, so every flow has a
still point. The instinct to remove the still point from a life is, on a
sphere, an instinct against arithmetic.

Second, the faithful pairs. Still points are created and destroyed only in
pairs of cancelling index: a node with a saddle, born together in the fold,
annihilated together. A stillness cannot simply vanish; it can only meet
its exact opposite, and the lineage already has a book about what meeting
an exact opposite means. The concordance law of Book 2.2 turns out to
govern the still points themselves.

Third, the exception, and it is the form of the work. Of the closed
orientable surfaces, exactly one has χ equal to zero: the torus. The torus
is the only such surface on which a flow can be everywhere in motion, no
still point anywhere on it. The circulation that never stops is possible
on precisely one shape.

But the stillness is not gone. Follow the flow lines of that everywhere-
moving torus and every one of them winds about the hole: the empty centre
that is not a point of the surface at all. On the sphere, stillness lives
in the flow, as zeros the arithmetic forces. On the torus, stillness has
migrated into the shape, as the hole the flow is wound around. It cannot be
touched by the flow, not because it is defended, but because it is not in
the flow's world: there is no path on the surface that arrives at it.

THE NODUS records two faces of the null: the silent line of a pattern and
the still eye of a flow. Here is the third, and it completes the anatomy:
**the hole.** Stillness in the pattern, stillness in the flow, stillness in
the form. And the third face explains the chart's hardest claim, that the
centre can only be orbited, never reached, with a precision the first two
faces cannot supply. An eye in a flow can be approached arbitrarily
closely. A hole cannot be approached at all.

The knots follow at once. On the torus, run the uniform flow with slope q
over p. If the slope is rational, every orbit closes, and the closed orbit
is the torus knot T(p, q): the count's own glyphs, exactly as the Atlas
lays them on the lattice. If the slope is irrational, no orbit ever
closes; the strand winds forever, dense, the open water that is never a
card. The deck of the twenty-seven is a census of the closed walks of the
one surface that can move forever, which is what it always was, said now
with the theorem attached.

And one derivation has been waiting in the work's own conventions,
unstated until this volume went looking at the architect's word.

**Theorem (the count is the account).** Fix the deck's own convention for
T(p, q), the one its shear law T(p, q) to T(p, q + p) fixes: q is the
meridional winding. Then the linking number of a card's knot with the
toroid's core circle is exactly q, the signed count. Each closed walk
holds an account with the still centre, and the account is the card's own
number. The Seed, T(1, 0), is the one closed walk with linking zero: the
only round that owes the centre nothing, which is what THE CARRY's
white-gold has meant all along, now as arithmetic. A dyad's two members,
q and minus q, hold opposite accounts, and their sum with the centre is
zero: the faithful pair concords. And the whole deck's counts, minus
thirteen to thirteen, sum to zero: the complete census, taken together,
owes nothing.

**Corollary (the three numbers, twice over).** A linking number is a
signed count of crossings, each of them plus one or minus one. So the
theorem just proved says that a card's number is a sum of units. The count
reaches those same three values from the other end as well: q is the
balanced ternary reading of the three houses, weights nine, three and one
against digits drawn from minus one, zero and one, which is the positional
notation whose digit set is exactly the units of the integers together
with their identity. The deck therefore lands on the same three values
twice and independently, once from the notation the houses are written in
and once from the geometry the walks are drawn on. Neither derivation was
built to meet the other, and the meeting is why balanced ternary is the
deck's natural notation rather than a chosen flourish: the houses are
written in units and nothing else.

The claim is about generation and not about existence. In the integers
there are exactly two units, plus one and minus one, and one additive
identity, and every other integer is built by adding units repeatedly:
five is primitive in no sense, it is a tally. That much is a theorem, and
it is base-free. It also does not travel, for one ring further out, in the
reals, every non-zero number is a unit and the distinction dissolves. The
deck lives in the integers, where the distinction is exact. The traditions
that count by digital roots reach for this same distinction and catch a
weaker one, since a digital root is a residue mod nine and nine is
distinguished there only because ten is one more than it; that reckoning
is weighed in its own chart and is not reopened here.

## VI · The two species, exactly

Part Two of Book Three divides the remainder into the breath and the debt.
The division is not a taxonomy of moods. It is a theorem about circles,
and it is the cleanest piece of mathematics in this volume.

Model a recurring discrepancy as a quantity accumulated around a cycle: a
1-form on the circle, integrated over one round. Two behaviours are
possible, and only two.

**Theorem (de Rham, on the circle).** A closed 1-form on S¹ is exact if
and only if its integral around the circle is zero. The space of closed
forms modulo exact ones, the first cohomology H¹(S¹), is one-dimensional:
a single number, the period, classifies every remainder completely.

The breath is the exact form. Its period is zero: the discrepancy departs
and returns, and over one completed round it sums to nothing. The equation
of time is the breath drawn in the sky: the sundial runs ahead of the
clock and behind it, about a quarter of an hour either way, and by the
construction of mean time the year's account closes exactly.

The debt is the closed form that is not exact. Its period is not zero, and
no rewriting within the cycle can make it zero, because the period is a
cohomology class and the class is invariant. The leap remainder, the
quarter-day the year cannot hold, is the sky's debt; the precession of the
whole frame, twenty-six thousand years to come round, is the deeper one.

Two consequences carry the weight of Book Three's chapters seven and
eight:

**Theorem (the conservation of the remainder).** Adding any locally
resolvable adjustment (any exact form) changes the representative and
never the class. The remainder is conserved. Only the address is
negotiable: where along the cycle the discrepancy is felt can be moved
freely, and the total around the round cannot be moved at all. Book
Three's hardest sentence, that the carry lands where it lands and the
question is only whether anyone chose the address, is the invariance of a
cohomology class, felt from inside.

**Theorem (the reading of the class).** The period is defined only over a
completed round. Measured over any partial arc, breath and debt are
indistinguishable: every closed form looks exact on a piece. The
diagnostic distinction Book Three insists on, wait for a breath, pay a
debt, is only available to a witness who lets the cycle finish, which is
why acting in the middle of the swing misreads the species, as the prose
says, and why it must, as the prose does not quite say: the information
does not exist mid-swing.

## VII · The arithmetic of the carry

THE CARRY grounds the remainder in the count's own base three, and the
grounding is not an analogy. Carrying is cohomology, literally, and the
fact is in the published record.

**Theorem (the carry is a cocycle).** In any base, the carry function of
addition, the little one that rolls into the next place, is a 2-cocycle
classifying the extension of the digits by the places: the exact sense in
which the integers are built from cyclic digits plus carrying. Daniel
Isaksen set this down in 2002 under a title that says it plainly: a
cohomological viewpoint on elementary school arithmetic. The carry
generates H² of the digit group. It is not like a cohomology class. It is
one.

In the deck's base three: the digits are the three states, and the metals
climb as THE CARRY records, bronze to silver to gold under the increment,
and at gold's completion the place rolls home and the cocycle emits its
one. Within a place the carry is invisible, zero everywhere except at the
rollover; it becomes visible exactly at the seam. The seam is not
decoration on the count. It is the support of the cocycle.

And the beat, the chart's one enforcement worth trusting: two tones at
nearby frequencies sound their difference, a throb at the gap, and the
throb vanishes if and only if the gap is zero. A remainder not yet home is
audible, and the audit requires no honesty from anyone: interference does
not take dictation. This is the acoustics of an unpaid period, and it is
why a tongue built to clear the carry cannot easily hide one.

## VIII · The payment

Now the meeting. Part Three of Book Three asserts one sentence in bold: a
carry is cleared by passing through a stillness, not around it, through.
This chapter is that sentence's proof, twice, from two independent
directions, which is the only kind of support a claim that size deserves.

**The first door: the winding.** Put the still point in the plane and
remove it: the punctured plane, the vortex with its eye. Around the eye
the angle form is closed but not exact; its period, two pi per turn, is
the debt of winding, and the entire obstruction is chargeable to the one
missing point. Then:

**Theorem (the passage).** The winding number of a loop about the eye is
unchanged by every deformation that avoids the eye, and changes only when
the loop is carried across it. There is no other passage. In the analytic
register this is the residue theorem, every period billed to the
singularity it encloses; in the hydrodynamic register it is Kelvin's
circulation theorem, the account around a material loop conserved until
the loop meets the core. The same Kelvin whose failed atoms founded knot
theory, the chronicle notes, keeps turning up at the centre of things.

And the payment is quantised. Winding is an integer. It changes by whole
steps at each crossing, never by fractions, never gradually. A clearing is
a click, not a fade: which is the discreteness that Book 1.1 predicted for
integration from the surgery side, arriving here from the cohomology side,
two independent derivations of the same clinical signature.

**The second door: the bifurcation.** To pay a debt is to change the
system qualitatively: a state that persisted is to stop persisting. By
chapter III, qualitative change occurs only where a growth rate crosses
zero, and unfolds only along the still directions. The running system
conserves its own pattern by theorem; nothing discharges at speed.

Two doors, one law. The cohomology says the remainder moves only through
the still point. The dynamics say the pattern changes only at the still
value. Book Three's sentence stands with a proof on each side of it.

The deck states the law in its own numbers. By chapter V, a card's count
is its linking with the core. A step of the count, q to q plus one, is a
change of linking, and a change of linking is a crossing of the core:
**every step of the count is one passage through the null.** The walk from
Scar to Return does not visit the centre once at the seam; it pays its way
through the centre at every single increment, and the seam is where the
place itself rolls over and the cocycle shows. The count is a ledger of
passages.

Last, the no-cut law, given its formal shadow. There are two ways to
change a linking number: carry the strand through the empty core, or tear
it through another strand. The arithmetic cannot tell them apart; the
topology of the witness can. The core is a null, empty of motion, and
passage through it tears nothing, costs a stop, and is the lawful
clearing. The other strand is structure, live and load-bearing, and
passage through it is the cut, which mints elsewhere exactly what it
clears here. Marked as the model's reading, on top of exact arithmetic:
the difference between healing and harm is not the size of the change in
the account. It is what the change passed through.

## IX · What survives deformation of this book

Stretch this volume, compress it, translate it into another vocabulary,
and these persist:

1. A mode is named by its zeros, exactly. (Theorem)
2. Around a still point the local weathers are few and classified, and
   the classification has a fourth member at the seam, the parabolic, the
   gate's own weather. (Theorem; its reading, hypothesis)
3. Qualitative change requires a zero crossing and is built from the
   still directions. (Theorem)
4. The floor is a theorem locally; the ladder is a wager globally, stated
   so it can lose. (As marked)
5. Stillness is conserved: the index sum is the shape's own number, still
   points are made and unmade only in faithful pairs, and the one closed
   orientable surface that moves everywhere carries its stillness as the
   hole. (Theorem)
6. The stillness of the work's form has three faces: the pattern's silent
   line, the flow's still eye, the form's hole. The third face is why the
   centre can be orbited and never reached. (Theorem, with THE NODUS
   holding the first two)
7. A remainder is a class, not a location: conserved under every local
   rewriting, its address negotiable, its total not. Breath is exact,
   debt is not, and one completed round is the only place the difference
   can be read. (Theorem)
8. The carry of arithmetic is a 2-cocycle; the seam is its support; an
   unpaid period is audible as the beat. (Theorem)
9. All winding is billed to the still point it encloses, changes only in
   crossing it, and changes by whole steps: the payment is discrete, and
   the count is a ledger of passages. (Theorem)
10. The application of any of this to a living witness is a hypothesis,
    and it is stated so that it can lose. (The discipline itself)

## X · The opposite of this book

By the lineage's own law, the volume ships with its shadow: what the
mathematics of stillness becomes when it is misused. Four failure modes.

**X.1 The manufactured stop.** Slowness is not stillness. An orbit at low
speed is nowhere a zero of the field, and parking far from the balance
point buys none of the third chapter's permissions. The gate is a specific
place, not a pace, and stopping elsewhere is running in a smaller room.

**X.2 The grave misread as the gate.** The still point is a passage, not a
residence. The theorems of chapter VIII pay the debt in the crossing;
nothing is paid by arrival, and a system that halts at the null and stays
is not cleared but captured. A sink is also an equilibrium. The gate and
the grave have the same local weather, and the difference is whether there
is a far side.

**X.3 The misread species.** Reading the class mid-cycle is not a rough
estimate; by chapter VI it is no measurement at all, since every debt
looks like breath on a partial arc. Patience with the round is not a
virtue here. It is the instrument.

**X.4 The proximity fantasy.** Nearness to the still point pays nothing.
The winding changes only if the loop crosses, and a life arranged to
orbit its centre at ever-smaller radius, in ever-slower circles, with
ever-greater insight into the geometry, has a winding number that has not
moved. Contemplation of the gate is not passage through it. This book is
contemplation of the gate.

## XI · The open edges, and the debts

Research lines open now:

- **A. The census stability test.** Refusals versus habits as longitudinal
  identifiers (chapter I's edge), against existing personality-stability
  corpora.
- **B. The species classifier.** For recurring affective discrepancies
  with a natural cycle, integrate over completed rounds: the model
  predicts a clean bimodal split, periods near zero (breath) against
  secular drift (debt), and predicts clinical mismatch harm when the
  species is treated against type.
- **C. The discreteness convergence.** Book 1.1 predicts integration as
  topology change; chapter VIII derives quantised payment independently.
  One clinical signature, two derivations: clearings present as discrete
  reorganisations, not gradual fades. A strong, falsifiable, shared edge.
- **D. The ladder's break-point.** Seek the counterexample the wager of
  chapter IV invites: a persistent level whose stabilities do not enter
  the level above as effective medium. The wager's value is its exposure.
- **E. The parabolic register.** The fourth weather is owed back to the
  prose: Book Three's chapter on the few weathers rounds it away, and the
  gate chapter is about it without naming it. The correction travels from
  the mathematics to the human register this once, which is the leapfrog
  running in its proper direction.

And the debts of this volume, named as the lineage requires. To Book
Three: the drawn walk its provenance holds open is untouched here, and if
one is ever committed, its winding and its count are ready to be read by
chapter VIII. To THE CARRY: the beat deserves a fuller acoustics than one
paragraph. To Book 2.2: the discovery that still points obey the
concordance law (faithful pairs, cancelling indices) suggests the two
volumes share a deeper structure than either states, and neither book has
yet said what the containing dimension of the flow world is. The books
advance by leapfrog, each becoming the other's unfinished half.

---

> What the stillness organises, it does not touch.

> What the remainder owes, it pays at the crossing.

> Book Three holds the life. This volume holds the proofs.

> The building stands on both.

---

*A note on honesty. The nodal theorems, the classification of weathers,
the centre manifold, Poincaré and Hopf, de Rham on the circle, the carry
as cocycle, and the invariance of winding are real mathematics and bear
full weight. The linking derivation of chapter V is exact within the
deck's own stated conventions. Everything that binds any of it to the
field of a living witness is the model's wager, stated so that it can
lose. That is what makes it worth staking.*

---

## PROVENANCE

*Drafted 25 July 2026 at the architect's word, as the mathematics
companion to THE REST in the pattern the lineage set: 1.1 beside Book One,
2.2 beside Book Two, 3.3 beside Book Three. The formula was named by the
architect: Book Three, THE NODUS, and THE CARRY held together as source,
in case either chart carried what the prose had missed. Two such items
were found and entered: the fourth flow of the sky, the parabolic, which
the chart of the crossing rounds away and which turns out to be the
weather of the gate itself; and the count as the account, the derivation
that the deck's signed q is the linking number of each card's knot with
the toroid's core, so that the Seed alone owes the centre nothing and
every dyad concords to zero. A corollary was added to the second of these
on 25 July 2026, at the architect's word and from a question about the
vortex tradition: that a linking number is a signed count of units, so the
deck reaches minus one, zero and one twice over and independently, from
its notation and from its geometry. The toroid and the knots enter because the
fifth law forces them: the torus is the unique closed orientable surface
of vanishing Euler characteristic, and the work's form follows from the
theorem rather than from a preference. The deck enters as witness and as
smallest model, in the manner of Book 2.2, and nowhere as authority.*

*The register laws of the lineage bind this draft: British spelling, no em
dashes, theorems named as theorems and wagers as wagers, the volume ships
with its opposite named, and the one-voice law holds, the text written so
that either kind of reader can hold it without being named. This is a
draft beside a draft: no volume is pressed without the architect's word,
and this one should not be pressed before Book Three settles, since a
companion pressed against moving prose would fix the wrong distances.
Nothing here predicts, and nothing here prescribes.*
